runbooks.title: Many users cannot use Microsoft 365
runbooks.summary: Establish the affected scope before changing individual devices.
steps: Record the affected service, tenant, users, first observed time and business impact.
Open the correct tenant’s admin center, then Health and Service health. Match the reported symptoms to active incidents.
Record the advisory or incident ID, Microsoft’s latest update and any stated workaround. Distinguish vendor estimates from your own observations.
Link affected tickets to one incident, assign an owner and agree the next customer update time.
When the vendor reports recovery, test with an affected user and record the result before closing the incident.
runbooks.escalateWhen: No matching incident, increasing impact or recovery tests still fail.

runbooks.title: Outlook cannot send or receive
runbooks.summary: Separate mailbox service, identity and local-client problems.
steps: Capture the exact error, Outlook version, user, time and whether one or many people are affected.
Check service health and try the same mailbox in Outlook on the web. Confirm licensing and connectivity.
If the web mailbox works, check client updates and run the available Outlook connectivity diagnostic.
If the web mailbox also fails, review the account and tenant rather than repeatedly rebuilding the client.
Use profile repair only after the findings support it; protect locally stored data. Retest sending and receiving with a traceable test message.
evidence: Error screenshot with sensitive content redacted
runbooks.escalateWhen: Multiple users fail, authentication is suspicious or mail remains unavailable after the scoped fix.

runbooks.title: Teams sign-in fails
runbooks.summary: Use the failure code and account context to choose the next check.
steps: Record the error code, account, client version and UTC time. Confirm the intended work tenant.
Compare web and desktop sign-in and check Microsoft 365 service health.
Run the available Teams sign-in diagnostic with an authorised admin account.
Review connectivity and the matching Entra sign-in event; a Conditional Access block needs policy-owner review.
Update the client when needed. Apply a documented client repair only after identity and service issues are excluded, then retest.
runbooks.escalateWhen: The failure involves access policy, unfamiliar activity or more than one service.

runbooks.title: Teams call audio or video is poor
runbooks.summary: Correlate user symptoms with meeting and participant telemetry.
steps: Record the meeting, participant, time window, device, connection type and exact symptom.
Open the meeting in the Teams admin center and review the affected participant’s session.
Compare device, network and media indicators. One highlighted value alone does not establish the root cause.
Compare another headset or an approved stable connection; change one variable per test.
Repeat a short call, capture the result and route recurring network or endpoint patterns to the responsible team.
runbooks.escalateWhen: Several users or sites show the same failure, or evidence remains inconclusive.

runbooks.title: A user cannot sign in
runbooks.summary: Locate the failed authentication event before resetting access.
steps: Capture the username, application, error, device and UTC timestamp. Verify the tenant.
In Entra ID, open Monitoring and health, then Sign-in logs. Filter by the user, time and failed status.
Review the failure reason, authentication details and applicable Conditional Access results.
Record the correlation ID and error code. Use the documented error lookup to identify the correct next action.
Apply an authorised, scoped fix and confirm a new successful event. Escalate suspicious sign-ins for security investigation.
runbooks.escalateWhen: Risk indicators appear, policy changes are needed or privileged accounts are involved.

runbooks.title: Lost phone or MFA registration problem
runbooks.summary: Recover the verified user’s access without creating an unmanaged bypass.
steps: Verify the requester using the organisation’s approved identity-verification procedure and record the ticket.
Review registered methods and recent sign-in activity with the appropriate authentication-administration role.
Use the approved recovery path, such as managed re-registration or Temporary Access Pass where configured.
If compromise is suspected, follow the incident procedure and revoke affected sessions as authorised.
Have the user register a supported method and test sign-in. Record which methods changed, without storing secrets or recovery codes.
runbooks.escalateWhen: Identity cannot be verified, a privileged user is affected or compromise is suspected.

runbooks.title: A Windows device will not enrol
runbooks.summary: Check eligibility and the exact error before resetting the device.
steps: Capture device ID, OS version, ownership type, user, timestamp and enrolment error code.
Check the assigned licence, supported OS, enrolment permissions, restrictions and device limits.
Verify connectivity, proxy requirements and the device’s clock and time zone.
Check whether the device is already enrolled or associated with another management configuration. Review relevant logs.
Apply the documented fix for that error and verify successful enrolment and policy check-in. Obtain approval before any reset or wipe.
runbooks.escalateWhen: A reset is proposed, ownership is unclear or the same error affects multiple devices.

runbooks.title: Investigate a Defender alert
runbooks.summary: Build an evidence-based incident timeline and record response decisions.
steps: Open the alert and record its ID, severity, detection time, affected device and user.
Review the alert story, related incidents, entities and process or event timeline.
Correlate the behaviour with approved work and other evidence. Treat an alert as a signal requiring investigation.
Use response actions under the agreed incident procedure. Document the reason, actor and time for containment decisions.
Record the investigation outcome and supporting evidence, then classify and resolve the alert only when the criteria are met.
runbooks.escalateWhen: Active compromise, critical assets, lateral movement or uncertain containment requires the incident lead.

runbooks.title: SharePoint says Access denied
runbooks.summary: Distinguish identity, permissions and service availability.
steps: Capture the exact site or file URL, user identity, error and time. Avoid copying document contents into the ticket.
Confirm that the browser is using the intended account; compare a private browsing session.
Ask the site owner to check the user’s effective permissions and any intended access expiry.
For wider failures, check service health. For throttling or a waiting page, follow the documented retry behaviour.
Apply the minimum approved permission change, then test the original resource and record the result.
runbooks.escalateWhen: Access approval is missing, broad permissions are proposed or many users are affected.

runbooks.title: OneDrive files are not syncing
runbooks.summary: Identify the sync state and protect unsynchronised work.
steps: Record the sync icon, error, account and affected files. Identify any unsynchronised local changes.
Check that the correct account is signed in and compare the file in the web interface.
Check storage space, quota, paused sync and connectivity. Use the official icon-specific troubleshooting path.
Update the client when needed. Before unlinking or resetting, confirm local work is protected and explain that a new sync may take time.
Use a small test file to verify upload and download, then confirm the affected files are consistent.
runbooks.escalateWhen: Unsynchronised work is at risk, storage limits persist or the issue affects many users.

runbooks.title: A message did not arrive
runbooks.summary: Trace the message before changing mail policies.
steps: Collect sender, recipient, approximate send time, timezone, message ID and any non-delivery report.
In the Exchange admin center, open Mail flow and Message trace using an authorised role.
Search the narrow time window and review whether the message was received, rejected, deferred or delivered.
Inspect processing events and the relevant policy or connector. Delivered status does not prove the recipient read the message.
Make a scoped, approved correction if required and retest. Document the trace result and actual delivery outcome.
runbooks.escalateWhen: The issue involves a security policy, widespread delay or an external sender’s configuration.

runbooks.title: SPF, DKIM or DMARC fails
runbooks.summary: Check the sender and alignment before editing DNS.
steps: Obtain the original message headers and identify the legitimate sending service and expected domain.
Read Authentication-Results to separate SPF, DKIM and DMARC results and inspect alignment with the visible From domain.
Check the published SPF TXT, DKIM selector records and DMARC TXT record against the provider’s configuration.
Record the existing DNS values, obtain change approval and apply only the required correction.
Allow for DNS caching, send another message and recheck headers. Investigate forwarding or gateways when they change authentication behaviour.
runbooks.escalateWhen: A third-party sender, gateway or unexplained source requires the mail-security owner.

verification.result: HTTP 403 from both research browser and direct HTTP request; do not claim connected

newsImplementation.fetchPolicy: Fetch only enabled, server-configured HTTPS feed URLs; do not accept arbitrary URLs from the browser.
newsImplementation.contentPolicy: Display text-only headlines and source links; discard scripts and feed HTML. Do not republish full articles.
newsImplementation.freshnessPolicy: Keep publisher publication time separate from the successful fetch time. Label cached or unavailable results honestly; never relabel an old article as newly published.
newsImplementation.languagePolicy: Use the configured English feeds and check the channel or entry language where provided. Exclude non-English entries.
newsImplementation.failurePolicy: Use the last successful cache with its original fetch timestamp, or show a news-unavailable state if no successful cache exists.
